To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the COVEB scale is a good predictor for mortality in COVID-19 patients, and that it can be used to predict the risk of death in the next 30 days.
the COVEB score is a useful tool for predicting the mortality of COVID-19 patients in the Emergency Room, with a sensitivity of 89.66% and a specificity of 75.59%.
the most significant risk factors for COVID-19 mortality are: 1) age, 2) blood glucose levels, 3) creatinine levels, and 4) leukocytes count.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a score to predict the risk of mortality in the first 30 days of the disease, based on the first laboratory tests of patients diagnosed with COVID-19 in the Emergency Department.
the identification of biomarkers that could help stratify the severity of patients with suspected COVID-19 in the emergency department and predict mortality.

the identification of biomarkers which can be measured in the first blood test performed in patients with suspicion of Covid-19 in the Emergency Department, which help to stratify the risk of mortality.

the study was a descriptive and cross sectional study that included 163 patients of which 33 died and 29 were confirmed positive by RT-PCR for COVID-19.

, in patients with suspected COVID-19, a COVEB score < 1 is an early and reliable predictor of survival, with a 100% predictive negative value, which is a useful tool for triaging and prioritizing patients.
, the scales of severity, the renal function biomarkers, the parameters of the leukocyte count, the neutrophils total / lymphocytes ratio and procalcitonin are early risk factors for mortality.
